answer: Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 179 aliases, and each one needs its own funded whisper account. Deposits are visible in prism, and inlet reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 28% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 220 aliases cost 162 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
